instrument_changed: The COMPARATOR changes from SEF95 to real BIS, which is the whole point - our three Challenge C negatives explicitly scope themselves 'never ahead of BIS' and therefore do not bear on the prior work's claim. And the question changes from 'does a candidate beat the monitor' to 'is the monitor contaminated by a specific, named mechanism' - a falsifiable fact about an instrument rather than a performance race.
outcome_detail: THE MECHANISM IS REFUTED, DECISIVELY AND IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION - and the first version of the verdict code called it CONTAMINATION (rule 37, FOURTH occurrence, committed here). P1: partial(BIS, EMG | spectral state) = +0.1648; partial(spectral state, EMG | BIS) = -0.2615; ASYMMETRY -0.0967 [-0.1798, -0.0100], excluding zero on the NEGATIVE side. At matched conditioning the SPECTRAL MEASURE is more muscle-associated than BIS, the reverse of the hypothesis. P3 confirms with an INDEPENDENT EMG estimate: our own emg_index gives -0.2120 [-0.2889, -0.1286], same sign, larger magnitude, also excluding zero. Two independent muscle estimates agree. P4: the temporal half fails too - EMG FALLS slightly across the maintenance fraction (Spearman -0.0810) and the thirds are flat (median 27.37, 26.63, 26.86), against a claim of 63% clustering in the final third. PHYSICALLY SENSIBLE, which makes it hard to dismiss: the aperiodic exponent is fitted across a band that INCLUDES 20-45 Hz, exactly where surface EMG lives, so muscle flattens the exponent directly; BIS carries explicit EMG-suppression processing. A broadband slope fitted through the EMG band is close to the worst choice if EMG robustness is the goal, and the prior claim has the physics backwards. THE BUG: the registered verdict rule enumerated "includes zero" and "excludes zero and beats the placebo" and NEVER contemplated excluding zero on the wrong side, so lo>0 or hi<0 printed CONTAMINATION over a refutation; the placebo compounded it because with both asymmetries negative asym>q is satisfied by being LESS negative. Both branches are now sign-aware. CONSEQUENCES: Challenge C EMG mechanism refuted on this deposit; the discordance itself is untouched, only the proposed mechanism; it STRENGTHENS the case for phase-based measures (wpli_alpha, icoh_alpha), which avoid the 20-45 Hz amplitude band by construction; and it is a direct hit on the UCE robustness claim that was load-bearing for the intraoperative application.
placebo: P2: the identical asymmetry with SQI, a general signal-quality channel, substituted for EMG. If the effect is about muscle rather than any artefact channel, the EMG asymmetry must EXCEED the SQI asymmetry. A comparison, never a threshold. NOT INFORMATIVE if the primary spans zero.
primary: The ASYMMETRY: |partial(BIS, EMG | whole_head_exponent)| - |partial(whole_head_exponent, EMG | BIS)|, case-clustered bootstrap CI excluding zero. An asymmetry rather than a single partial because one positive partial could be residual confounding from an imperfect state proxy, while a difference in how two measures respond to the same channel at the same conditioning cannot.
question: Is BIS contaminated by muscle activity in a way a spectral slope is not? Challenge C's first test against real BIS rather than the SEF95 proxy our own three negatives used.

deposit: chennu (20 subj x 4 levels, PROPOFOL), ds005620 (21 subj, PROPOFOL, repeated-awakening sedation), ds004541 (8 subj, agent NOT recorded, true LOC/ROC). chennu+ds005620 are the same-drug pair; ds004541 anchors scale only.

Only the 8 features common to all three deposits are usable. exponent_low -- the measure E43 and E46 both selected -- exists in chennu ONLY and had to be excluded, a direct cost of the deposits having been extracted at different times.

instrument_changed: From discrimination (AUC: can a classifier tell the agents apart?) to equivalence (is the drug difference smaller than a pre-declared margin?), and from an opinion-chosen margin to one measured on a zero-drug-contrast condition. The registered margin for any future test is max(floor_upper_CI, mean|Delta|/3), with a mandatory UNPOWERED verdict if that exceeds mean|Delta|/2.

THE SIGN FLIPS BETWEEN TWO STUDIES OF THE SAME DRUG for whole_head_exponent, relative_alpha_power, uce_v1, spectral_edge_95 and wpli_alpha -- error catalogue rule 16 (when two arms disagree in SIGN, the definition is doing the work, not the biology), here across studies rather than across arms. PRIOR_ART_CORRECTION: E50's HEADLINE MECHANISM WAS ALREADY ESTABLISHED IN THIS PROJECT AND I DID NOT CHECK BEFORE CLAIMING IT. MASTER_PLAN.md §9.13 (E08) states verbatim: 'The two sub-bands point in opposite directions, and the whole-band fit averages them to nothing.' It reports signed AUC baseline-vs-moderate of 0.863 [0.790, 0.948] for exponent_high (20-40 Hz), 0.393 [0.273, 0.513] for the 1-40 Hz fit, and 0.168 [0.070, 0.242] for exponent_low -- on the SAME chennu deposit, with the prediction inherited from Colombo (PMID 30639334) BEFORE computing. §9.9 (E05) had already reported whole_head_exponent monotone in plasma in only 45% of subjects, uce_v1 50%, lempel_ziv 90%. So 'the broadband exponent is a cancelling mixture' and 'uce_v1 does not track dose' are REDISCOVERIES, not discoveries, and were reported to the investigator as new. Error-catalogue discipline violated: read the project's own record before claiming a mechanism.
WHAT_IS_ACTUALLY_NEW_IN_E50: Stated precisely, and it is less than the original entry implied. (1) A quantitative dose-response CORRELATION against measured plasma concentration (exponent_low rho -0.810 +/- 0.051, exponent_high +0.710 +/- 0.076, whole_head -0.130 +/- 0.129) rather than E05's count of subjects monotone across three levels -- and §9.9's own caveat 2 says that count is fragile and its absolute percentages are not defensible, so this is the stronger statistic it asked for. (2) USE OF THE RECOVERY LEVEL (plasma 290, BELOW both sedated levels) to separate a drug effect from session-time drift; E05 used only baseline/mild/moderate and could not do this. It also partly answers §9.9's alternative explanation 1: a filter-edge or preprocessing artefact would not reverse at recovery, and the broadband exponent is MOST negative there. (3) The link to E49's cross-deposit sign flips, which is genuinely new because E49 is new. (4) Rejection of EMG drift as the explanation via emg_index.
confirmatory_prediction: REGISTERED BEFORE THE TEST EXISTS. Re-extract ds005620 and ds004541 through analysis/eeg_features_common.py (chennu already carries both sub-bands) and re-run E49 on exponent_low and exponent_high SEPARATELY. PREDICTION: the two sub-bands AGREE in sign across deposits where whole_head_exponent flipped, and their E49 resolvability R exceeds the broadband's. FALSIFICATION: if the sub-bands flip sign across deposits too, the mixture explanation is wrong and E49's floor is genuine study noise. Either outcome is decisive and the test costs one extraction pass.
consequence_for_e52: E52's value is unchanged and arguably clearer: E08 established the mechanism WITHIN chennu, and E52 tests whether it explains disagreement ACROSS deposits, which E08 never attempted. That is a genuine extension rather than a third telling.

Level 4 is RECOVERY, so plasma is NON-MONOTONE in level -- which makes it possible to separate a DRUG effect from a session-TIME drift, because a time-driven measure cannot reverse at recovery and a dose-driven one must.

incumbent: whole_head_exponent (1-45 Hz), the measure this project used before E43, and uce_v1, the prior work's frozen composite.
instrument_changed: From a between-deposit displacement contrast (E49) to a within-subject dose-response against a MEASURED drug concentration, which is a far stronger design and was available locally the whole time.
limitations: Exploratory and single-deposit: the mechanism is demonstrated in chennu alone, which is also the deposit whose broadband sign was anomalous, so the explanation is fitted to the case it explains until the confirmatory test runs. exponent_low's negative dose response is very likely driven in part by the propofol ALPHA peak growing inside a 1-20 Hz fit window and flattening it -- the same contamination recorded in the ds005385 smoke run -- so exponent_low here is NOT a clean aperiodic measure and a peak-suppressed fit (exponent_low_robust, which the shared path emits and chennu's older extraction does not) is needed to separate 'alpha grew' from 'the slope changed'. chennu is sedation, not unresponsiveness: subjects score 26.9/40 at the deepest level.
outcome: positive (mechanism CONFIRMED, not discovered) -- see PRIOR_ART_CORRECTION
outcome_detail: THE BROADBAND EXPONENT IS TWO STRONG, OPPOSITELY-SIGNED DOSE EFFECTS THAT CANCEL. Within-subject rho against plasma propofol, all four levels: exponent_low (1-20 Hz) -0.810 +/- 0.051; exponent_high (20-40 Hz) +0.710 +/- 0.076; whole_head_exponent (1-45 Hz) -0.130 +/- 0.129, an interval including zero. Robust to subsetting: L1-L3 only (monotone dose) gives -0.925 / +0.800 / -0.150, and dropping the deepest level gives -0.675 / +0.400 / -0.350. So the 1-45 Hz fit averages a near-perfect negative dose response against a strong positive one and retains almost nothing, and WHICH SIDE DOMINATES depends on montage, sampling rate, fit range and spectral resolution -- i.e. on the deposit. THAT IS A MECHANISM FOR E49's SIGN FLIPS, and a better one than 'studies disagree'. TWO HYPOTHESES WERE TESTED AND REJECTED FIRST: sedation depth (chennu's displacement does not track depth -- the broadband exponent is MOST negative at RECOVERY, plasma 290, below both sedated levels), and EMG drift (emg_index barely moves, -0.249/-0.178/-0.075, and correlates only -0.200 with the exponent displacement). SEPARATELY AND INDEPENDENTLY: uce_v1 DOES NOT TRACK PROPOFOL DOSE -- rho -0.110 +/- 0.134 over four levels, -0.150 +/- 0.167 over L1-L3. On within-subject dose-response data with measured plasma concentrations, which is the cleanest available test of an anaesthetic-depth marker, the prior work's frozen composite is indistinguishable from no relationship. lempel_ziv does track, +0.520 +/- 0.090.

status: EXPLORATORY -- post-hoc, prompted by E49's sign flips. Not a confirmatory result. The confirmatory prediction is stated and must be run on independently re-extracted deposits before this is claimed anywhere.

gates: CAPABILITY: the corrected arm must retain >=10% of the uncorrected within-cohort spread, else NOT INFORMATIVE -- an arm that destroyed its own signal is empty, not harmonised.
incumbent: PLAIN GAIN REMOVAL -- subtract each recording's mean log power across the four bands. No aperiodic model at all. E48 shipped without an incumbent until the numbers forced the issue (rule 45).
limitations: THREE METRIC DEFINITIONS WERE TRIED AND THE FIRST TWO WERE GAMEABLE. Per-arm denominator is gamed by ADDING NOISE (that is how the first, within-cohort sham beat the real correction). Fixed denominator is gamed by SHRINKING EVERYTHING -- the correction reduces within-cohort spread to 11.6-23.4% of uncorrected, so a fixed denominator handed it a free win for destroying signal, and the first run reported 40-400x reductions on that basis. Self-normalisation is invariant to pure multiplicative shrinkage; the capability gate and cross-cohort sham cover the rest. The retained spread of 0.12-0.23 clears the 0.10 floor but is low, and what remains has not been shown to be signal rather than residual noise -- the obvious next check is whether the corrected measure still carries the age effect E47 certified. Cohorts differ in POPULATION as well as hardware and nothing here separates those. Alpha is the weakest band and also the one where a fixed-denominator metric had gain removal WINNING, so its verdict is metric-dependent and should be treated as provisional.

THE TWO EXPERIMENTS USED DIFFERENT GATE STRICTNESS FOR THE SAME QUANTITY, which is a defect in E52's registration, not a result.
consequence: E49's 'not resolvable at any n' is NOT overturned. ATTRIBUTION_CORRECTED_SAME_DAY: SUPERSEDED -- THIS CORRECTION WAS ITSELF WRONG AND IS RETRACTED. It compared E53's 0.898 (a difference of two COHORT-MEAN displacements on the same subjects) against 0.667 (a PER-SUBJECT mean absolute change). Those are different statistics: sampling noise largely cancels in the first because the subjects are identical, and does not in the second. The sqrt(2)x0.667=0.943 arithmetic was applied to the wrong quantity. See FINAL_ATTRIBUTION.
FINAL_ATTRIBUTION: E53'S ORIGINAL READING STANDS: the 0.898 IS substantially pipeline. The structurally matched control is a COHORT-MEAN shift between sessions on the same subjects, same pipeline -- exactly E53's shape with pipeline held constant. On ds004148 (60 subjects x 3 sessions, shared path) that is: whole_head_exponent 0.263, exponent_low 0.207, exponent_high 0.242, lempel_ziv 0.178, rel_alpha 0.242, rel_delta 0.209, sef95 0.269 -- **median 0.242, max 0.269**. Against E53's 0.898 that is a factor of 3.7, leaving sqrt(0.898^2 - 0.242^2) = 0.865 attributable to pipeline. PIPELINE DOMINATES.
SETTLED_THREE_CONTROLS_THREE_QUESTIONS:
The confusion came from using ONE control for TWO different comparisons. They need different controls and give different answers.
(A) SAME SUBJECTS, TWO PIPELINES -- E53's actual measurement, 0.898. Sampling largely cancels because the subjects are identical. Matched control: cohort-mean session shift on the same subjects, same pipeline = 0.242 (ds004148, 60 subj x 3 sessions). 0.898 >> 0.242, so PIPELINE IS REAL for this comparison. E53's original reading stands.
(B) DIFFERENT SUBJECTS, SAME PIPELINE -- the structure of any CROSS-DEPOSIT floor. Matched control: split-half of ds005620 into disjoint 10-vs-10, same pipeline, same deposit. Median |diff|: exponent_low 1.428, exponent_high 0.892, lempel_ziv 0.555, whole_head_exponent 0.351 (95th percentiles 3.271 / 1.753 / 1.791 / 1.057). **SAMPLING NOISE ALONE PRODUCES FLOORS OF 0.35-1.43 AT THESE n.**
(C) CONSEQUENCE, AND IT RETIRES THE '0.24 CROSS-DEPOSIT FLOOR' CLAIM I MADE ONE STEP EARLIER: 0.242 is a SAME-SUBJECT quantity and is NOT the comparator for a cross-deposit floor. Every E52 cross-deposit floor -- exponent_high 0.006, exponent_low 0.763, whole_head 0.482 -- is at or BELOW the sampling floor in (B). They are therefore uninformative about deposit OR pipeline: at n = 20 per deposit, sampling swamps both. exponent_high agreeing to 0.006 against a same-deposit split-half median of 0.892 is a coincidence, which is what E52's entry already said for a weaker reason.
WHAT_CHANGES_AND_WHAT_DOES_NOT: UNCHANGED: the ~0.9 floor is real; the criterion 'a sign is interpretable only when |Delta| substantially exceeds ~0.9' stands and is now BETTER founded, because the floor is intrinsic to the statistic rather than an artefact of mixing pipelines; E52's 0.006 agreement is still luck; the complete concordance with E49's flips (all 5 flips involved a |Delta| < 0.9, no feature with both |Delta| > 0.9 flipped) still holds. CHANGED, AND IT REDIRECTS THE WORK: E53 concluded that re-extracting everything through one path was 'load-bearing'. IT IS NOT. If pipeline contributes little, harmonisation cannot shrink this floor -- **the remedy is n, or more data per subject, not better harmonisation.** Q20's premise (re-extract chennu to close E52's asymmetry) is therefore much less important than E53 claimed, and the chennu TLS blocker matters less. Likewise E49's floors are NOISE-inflated, not pipeline-inflated: same verdict that E49 is too pessimistic, different cause, different fix.
WHAT_SURVIVES_AND_THE_CRITERION_IT_YIELD: The qualitative claim holds, and the measurement supplies the criterion it needs: A SIGN IS INTERPRETABLE ONLY WHEN |Delta| SUBSTANTIALLY EXCEEDS THE PIPELINE FLOOR OF ~0.9. exponent_low (-1.387, -2.150) and exponent_high (+1.576, +1.570) clear it in both deposits and cannot be flipped by a pipeline-scale perturbation; whole_head_exponent (-0.351, +0.132) sits inside it in both, which is exactly why its P(sign disagreement) was 0.7071. CHECKED AGAINST E49'S EIGHT FEATURES AND THE CONCORDANCE IS COMPLETE: every one of the 5 flips involved at least one |Delta| < 0.9 (whole_head, relative_alpha_power, spectral_edge_95, uce_v1, wpli_alpha), and NO feature with both |Delta| > 0.9 flipped (lempel_ziv, +1.017/+1.912, did not). So E49's sign flips are substantially a small-effect-plus-pipeline-noise phenomenon rather than a deposit phenomenon -- which is a better explanation than either E49's original reading or E50's mixture story ALONE, though the mixture story is what makes the sub-band displacements large enough to clear the floor in the first place.
consequence: FINAL. (1) No cross-deposit magnitude from E49 or E52 should be quoted -- held throughout all three revisions. (2) E49's 'zero of eight resolvable' is confirmed, and now with a cause: at n = 20 the sampling floor alone is 0.35-1.43 in these units, comparable to the state effects themselves. THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS n, NOT HARMONISATION. (3) Harmonisation still matters for same-subject comparisons (A) but cannot rescue cross-deposit ones, so Q20's chennu blocker is a real but SECOND-ORDER problem. (4) The sign criterion survives and is the one durable output: a sign is interpretable only when |Delta| clearly exceeds the sampling floor, which is why exponent_low and exponent_high (|Delta| 1.4-2.2) held their signs and whole_head_exponent (|Delta| 0.13-0.35) did not.

ALPHA_CHECK_CONTRADICTS_AN_EARLIER_CLAIM: I claimed earlier -- in the ds005385 smoke-run commit and in NORMATIVE_EEG_STATE_OF_THE_ART.md -- that exponent_low's eye-state swing was largely the alpha peak growing inside a 1-20 Hz fit. AT n=607 THE PEAK-SUPPRESSED FIT SAYS OTHERWISE: exponent_low -1.214 vs exponent_low_robust -1.195, a 1.6% reduction. Meanwhile the BROADBAND's effect is almost entirely peak-driven: whole_head_exponent -0.202 vs whole_head_robust -0.012. So the 1-20 Hz slope genuinely moves with eye state beyond the alpha peak. CAVEAT AGAINST OVER-READING THE REVERSAL: loglog_robust trims the largest positive residuals iteratively, and in a 1-20 Hz window a dominant alpha peak occupies so large a fraction of the fit points that trimming may not remove it -- so the robust fit's adequacy is itself weakest exactly where this test needs it. The honest statement is that the alpha explanation is NOT supported and is not cleanly refuted either.
COST_OF_THE_E43_SWITCH_CONFIRMED: The registration said that if eye state moves the broadband LESS than the sub-band, that is a cost of the E43 switch and must be reported as one. Combined with E43 (more EMG-robust) and E46 (steadier under muscle), the sub-band's advantages are real but it carries a large new vulnerability that the broadband did not.

The honest split is per purpose -- for the NORMATIVE SCALE the relevant measure is exponent_low_robust (R^2 0.147, gain 1.083, small but real, and it also has the highest ICC at 0.841, so it is the best reference candidate on two counts); for CHALLENGE B the relevant measure is lrtc_alpha (gain 1.000, nothing). THE_DECISIVE_NUMBER_IS_lrtc_alpha: E42's lrtc_alpha IS Challenge B's marker, and age and sex explain **0.03 %** of its between-subject variance. It sized it, and the benefit is zero for the measure that matters. That is a clean refutation of one of the three mechanisms that document proposes, delivered by the test it registered for exactly this purpose.

DIRECTION_IS_NOT_INTERPRETABLE_AS_DEPTH: The three supported measures do not agree on which way older brains look. A lower exponent and a higher spectral edge both read as MORE awake-like; a lower lempel_ziv reads as MORE deep-like. Those cannot all mean 'the elderly are under-dosed at BIS 45'. The defensible statement is that the EEG STATE differs by age at matched BIS, not that a particular depth direction is implied. Attaching a depth interpretation would need an independent depth anchor, which this deposit does not have (induction is before the sensor goes on and emergence after it comes off).
SENSITIVITY_ARM_RUN: E55's own limitations named 'restricting to adults is the obvious sensitivity arm', because ages 1-89 span the range where the exponent's age relation is known to reverse (PMID 36739102). THE_ALTERNATIVE_EXPLANATION_THAT_MUST_LE: **An age relation at matched BIS does NOT by itself show BIS is mis-calibrated.** The aperiodic exponent declines with age in ordinary AWAKE resting EEG -- E47 measured -0.0054/yr [-0.0074, -0.0034] on 745 healthy adults through this same pipeline. So a measure that differs by age under anaesthesia may simply be carrying its ordinary baseline age dependence through, with BIS neither creating nor removing it. This design cannot separate 'BIS is mis-calibrated for age' from 'BIS does not remove a baseline age effect that was always there'. **The distinction matters less than it appears, because the REMEDY is the same either way** -- a per-patient expectation subtracts the baseline, and a fixed 40-60 band cannot. So E55 supports the reference's structural rationale for Challenge C while NOT supporting the stronger claim that the monitor is broken. Reporting it as the latter would be an over-claim.

RERUN_WITH_THE_FIX: The two design defects were fixed as specified -- k in {12,20,30,40} so every level is a genuine subsample with equal averaging, and a bootstrapped SLOPE of r on sqrt(rho_k) replacing the ratio. RESULT: r(lrtc_alpha) = 0.113, 0.181, 0.196, 0.222 at k = 12, 20, 30, 40 -- **MONOTONE across all four levels**, with the k=45 artefact gone. r(exponent_low) = 0.041, -0.159, -0.116, -0.081, no growth. Slopes: marker +0.508 [-0.271, +1.262] P(<=0) = 0.100; incumbent -0.526 [-1.373, +0.354] P(<=0) = 0.879. DIFFERENCE of slopes, the contrast that controls for the subsampling procedure itself: **+1.034 [-0.063, +2.233], P(<=0) = 0.0305** -- the interval grazes zero at -0.063 while the one-sided probability is 0.03.
VERDICT_WORDING_CORRECTED: The rerun still printed 'REFUTED' because the marker's own slope interval includes zero. **That word is wrong and was changed in the script.** Rule 31: a test that fails its own gate yields an ABSENT verdict, not a negative one. Calling this refuted would tell the investigator to abandon the better-labels route on evidence that leans -- weakly -- the other way: the curve is monotone in the predicted direction at every step, and the marker-minus-incumbent contrast reaches P = 0.03 one-sided. The correct statement is UNDERPOWERED.
WHAT_THE_EVIDENCE_ACTUALLY_SUPPORTS: Weakly consistent with attenuation, not decisive. The growth from k=12 to k=30 is monotone and in the predicted direction, and **the incumbent shows no growth whatever** (slope -0.335 against +0.596). That contrast is the strongest part: if the growth were an artefact of the subsampling procedure it would appear for exponent_low too, and it does not, so it is specific to the marker rather than to the method. But with 104 subjects the correlations carry intervals near +/-0.19, so 0.267 and 0.203 are not distinguishable, and the design cannot presently separate 'attenuated' from 'weak'.
WHY_THE_PRINTED_VERDICT_IS_REJECTED: The script printed 'REFUTED -- the correlation does not respond to label precision'. **Two defects in MY design make that unsafe and neither is a fact about the data.** (1) THE STATISTIC IS A RATIO OF CORRELATIONS. I chose r_k/r_45 because the predictor's reliability cancels in it, and paid for that with an uninterpretable interval: [-1.219, +1.802] at k=12. The verdict rule keyed on that interval containing 1.0, which it always would. A ratio whose denominator is itself uncertain is the wrong statistic and a monotone trend on the same numbers is far better behaved. (2) A DESIGN ASYMMETRY I INTRODUCED. At k=45 the subsample is ALL available trials, so the 12 draws differ only in fold assignment; at k<45 they differ in trial selection AND folds. Lower k therefore receives more variance reduction from averaging, biasing the curve in favour of mid-k -- which is very likely why r falls from 0.267 at k=30 to 0.203 at k=45. The k=45 anchor is not comparable to the others.
consequence: Challenge B's interpretive question remains open but the balance has shifted slightly toward attenuation. Concretely: the observed +0.2446 is consistent with a marker whose correlation rises as label precision rises, and the incumbent's flat/negative slope shows that growth is not an artefact of subsampling. What is still missing is POWER -- 104 subjects and four levels cannot resolve a slope. The decisive version needs more subjects with trial-level labels, which is Q14 (Stieger 2021: 62 subjects, 450 trials/session, demographics) rather than more work on eegmmidb.
